- If sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, reduce forecasted price by 1–2% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If model shows a sharp upward spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) followed by a forecasted decline, reduce the peak by 3–5% to avoid overshoot.  
- If forecast mean is > 10% above recent 18-day average, apply downward correction proportional to sentiment magnitude (e.g., -0.1×sentiment×10% of forecast).  
- If sentiment is positive but forecast is flat or declining, add 0.5–1% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates > 3% from 18-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent mean reversion trend.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), reduce forecast slope to avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment.
